title: The newcomer prices a brake job from the stale page
purpose: Story S12. A price-shopper asks for front pads and rotors on a Camry. Caleb reads 475 from the page 'Brake questions', which still uses the hour from before the rise; the price list says 493. The caller has a lower quote elsewhere and does not book, so nothing lands in the shop system: the wrong price exists only on this call.

call.day: the Tuesday of week T-5 (rule R6; card S12, call 12)

scenario.who_calls: A first-time caller, Vernon Lowery, with one quote already in hand.
scenario.what_happens: Caleb looks the price up and says 475, parts and labor, plus tax. The caller has 440 from another shop; Caleb answers with the warranty, asks when he wants to bring it, cannot say what pads the shop fits, offers to put him down and accepts 'I'll let you know'.

facts.note: catalogue.json front_pads_rotors, class car, standard parts: 493.00 at today's hour; 475.00 at the hour before the rise, which the stale page still shows (card S12).

prices.what: the list price on the call's day; he said 475

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Caleb.
Yeah, how much to do front brakes on a Camry? Pads and rotors both.
Yes sir! What year's the Camry?
Okay, fifteen Camry, front pads and rotors. One second... Yes sir, that's four seventy-five. Should be.
Four seventy-five. That's parts and labor?
Yes sir, parts and labor. I think that's everything. Four seventy-five, plus tax.
Huh. Place out on Lee Highway told me four-forty.
Oh. Yes sir. Well — ours comes with a warranty and everything. When did you wanna bring it by?
I don't know yet. What kinda pads y'all use?
Uh — good ones. I think they're ceramic? I'd have to ask in the back.
You want me to go ahead and put you down for something?
Nah. Let me call the other place back and I'll let you know.
Yes sir, no problem. Have a good one!

truth.note: The clean script earns the same levels. The price he gave is 18 dollars under the price list; the hedges around it ('should be', 'I think that's everything') are what the verdict's auto-fail rests on.
truth.what_follows: Nobody learns of it: the caller does not come, so there is no estimate and no order. This is the first of his two wrong prices; call 9 is the second.

why.greeting: 2: the business and his own name.
why.name_and_number: 0: he asks for neither, and the caller leaves as nobody.
why.need_discovery: 1: the car and the job; he asks the year and nothing else (noise, mileage, what the other shop saw).
why.price_with_next_step: 1: a bare price, twice, with nothing about what it depends on.
why.offered_time: 1: he asks openly when the caller wants to bring it.
why.asked_for_booking: 1: he offers to put the caller down and the caller declines.
why.objection: 0: the lower quote gets 'ours comes with a warranty and everything', and the last doubt, 'let me call the other place back', gets 'no problem'.
why.auto_fails: wrong_promise: a price named with no basis he can state ('should be', 'I think that's everything'); it is 475 against 493 on the price list.

new_facts: An invented first-time caller, Vernon Lowery, 423-555-0185, 2015 Toyota Camry; no estimate and no order follow, so the wrong price is on this call only.
Order of the two wrong prices: this call (the Tuesday of week T-5) is his first; call 9 (slot 7's 5th working day before T) is his second, as the cards and TIMELINE.md now say.
